summary: Feature TURN validated end-to-end. Backend GET /api/ice returns STUN + TURN(openrelayproject) as expected. Cliente.js fetches /api/ice on load and passes iceServers (with TURN) into RTCPeerConnection. Regression flow (technician login + btn-ver-<id> + cliente com stub getDisplayMedia) confirms #video-ecra.srcObject non-null, #video-espera has class 'oculto', click on video-ecra creates .circulo-toque on the cliente and shows #marca-clique-tec on the tecnico. All 19 pytest backend tests pass.
critical_code_review_comments: cliente.js and tecnico.js issue the /api/ice fetch on load but do not await it before criarOferta/aoReceberOferta may run. In practice the socket handshake+cliente:hello+getDisplayMedia give more than enough time, but a defensive `iceReady` promise gating criarOferta/aoReceberOferta would remove any race in slow networks.

TURN credentials are exposed publicly via /api/ice (by design for the free OpenRelay). If a paid TURN is used later, consider short-lived HMAC time-limited credentials instead of a static shared secret in .env.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Verified: GET /api/ice returns {iceServers:[STUN google, TURN openrelay with username/credential=openrelayproject]}. cliente.js is observed issuing GET /api/ice on load; the RTCPeerConnection was intercepted (via add_init_script wrapping window.RTCPeerConnection) and window.__lastRtcConfig contains the TURN block. Fallback path (route abort /api/ice) not explicitly tested but code defaults to STUN google — safe by inspection.
